name: Bajaj Finance Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest diversified non-bank lender (AUM Rs5.85 lakh cr at Sep 2026, +26.5% y/y): consumer durables/digital EMI, personal and business loans, SME, mortgages (via ~89%-owned Bajaj Housing Finance, AUM Rs1.5 lakh cr), vehicle and gold loans, deposits and cards. Q2 FY27 PAT Rs6,266cr (+29%), NII +24%. Promoter group (Bajaj Finserv) 54.7%. The board approved a Rs17,500cr capital raise on 2026-10-01/02 (QIP Rs11,700cr plus warrants Rs5,800cr to Bajaj Finserv) and management warned on margins in the Q2 call.

exposures.mechanism: Borrowings ~Rs4.3 lakh cr (model est., ~74% of AUM); ~35% floating (bank term loans, T-bill/repo-linked) = Rs1.5 lakh cr x 25bp = Rs376cr/yr; most assets fixed-rate (NIM compresses until repricing). vs PBT ~Rs27,000cr => -1.4%; fixed-rate funding reprices on rollover (~+10bp more over 12m) => -2.5% EBT; persistence 0.5 => ~-1.2; add P/E derating at 34x (long-duration growth stock) => ~-3. Management flagged margin pressure on the Q2 call.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening (The Hindu / SCC Online)
Q2 PAT Rs6,266cr +29%, NII +24%, AUM Rs5.85 lakh cr +26.5%, FY27 growth view lifted; margin warning on call (CNBC TV18 2026-10-21)

exposures.mechanism: 10y +25bp raises NBFC marginal funding (NCD/bond spreads over G-sec) and the cost of equity: at P/E 34x (P/B 5.6x), +25bp on COE ~ -2 to -3% of value.

+50bp spreads on market borrowings (~40% of funding = Rs1.7 lakh cr) = Rs860cr/yr = -3.2% of PBT, 50% pass-through to lending rates => -1.6%, persistence 0.5 -> -0.8; multiple effect (NBFC beta to credit spreads is high; stock fell 10% in a month before QIP) => -5.
+Rs1 lakh cr surplus liquidity lowers short-term funding (CP, bank lines) by ~5bp => +0.3% EBT; sentiment +0.5.
+3pp system credit growth lifts BFL's addressable demand; BFL AUM already +26.5% so incremental share gain small; AUM +1-1.5pp => PAT +2%, persistence 0.75 ... ~+2.

exposures.mechanism: +50bp credit cost on on-book AUM ~Rs5.5 lakh cr = Rs2,750cr = ~10% of PBT; persistence 0.5 => -5 (EV/equity ~1 as financial). Asset quality has been improving (analysts bullish on 'asset quality gains' 2026-10-21).

exposures.mechanism: Unsecured (personal, business, consumer-durable EMI, credit cards) ~35-40% of AUM = ~Rs2 lakh cr (model est.): +1pp delinquency x LGD 70% = Rs1,400cr = ~5% of PBT x persistence 0.5 = -2.5; plus sentiment/de-rating => -3.5. Pack t-stats not available for this factor.

evidence.note: Reuters: top NBFCs flag early stress in gold loans

exposures.mechanism: RBI has precedent of tightening on BFL itself (2023 ban on eCOM and Insta EMI card, model knowledge) and on NBFC risk weights/co-lending; a step costs ~-3 via growth/product restrictions and compliance.
Consumer durable/lifestyle/digital finance and personal-loan origination track urban consumption; +5pp urban demand => volumes +3-4%, credit cost down slightly => PAT +4%, persistence 0.6 => +2.5.
Bajaj Housing Finance (AUM Rs1.5 lakh cr, ~26% of group AUM; BFL holds ~89%, model knowledge) rides home-loan demand: +10% sales volume => BHFL disbursals +6% => group +1.5% PAT x 0.7 => ~+1.
Auto/2W/3W/tractor (mobility) finance ~8-10% of AUM; +10% auto volumes => +4% AUM growth in that segment => +0.4% group PAT; plus consumer-finance linkages => +1.
FIIs 19.8%, falling (21.3% in March); high-multiple growth financials are the first FPI-sensitive names; +2.
1y volatility 32% vs bank ~25%; market beta 1.24-1.29; VIX +5pts => -2% beyond beta.

Empirical +1.16 (t=1.7): proxies shared rate/liquidity beta rather than the small gold-loan book (<2% of AUM, model knowledge). Reuters (2026-10-21) flags gold-loan stress at top NBFCs, so a gold-price fall is a second-order credit risk. Shrunk to +0.3.

company_links.mechanism: w = % change in BAJFINANCE equity per +1% in BAJAJFINSV equity (source-equity-move units); parent is 51% owner and the warrant/QIP package ties group funding; BFL dominates parent value so reverse causality (BAJFINANCE->BAJAJFINSV) is far larger (see BAJAJFINSV).
